verdict.rationale: Pylon documents Connectors and administrator-defined Custom API tools that let its agents call internal or third-party API endpoints and take action outside Pylon, which covers the core of the agent acting through your APIs. The evidence never mentions refunds, order changes or subscription updates, and says nothing about per-action auth scoping. The MCP OAuth evidence covers outside AI tools reading Pylon data, not Pylon's agent calling your APIs, so it does not apply here. Missing for 10: documented per-action scoped auth or credential configuration for Custom API tools, concrete examples of transactional actions (refunds/orders/subscriptions), approval or guardrail controls on actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the agent takes real actions through my APIs — refunds, order changes, subscription updates — with scoped auth per action

citations.quote: an administrator can define a Custom API tool that agents can use to hit internal or third party API endpoints.
Connectors give Pylon agents access to external tools so they can search for context, retrieve information, and take action outside Pylon.
Support Agents can deflect customer questions using content, gather internal context for your team, and take action.
